hero.description: Borderfall is a turn-based strategy game where you conquer territory across nine eras, from ancient legions to a galactic frontier. Free to play in your browser.
hero.descriptionSuffix: Play real-time or async with friends, rivals, or AI.
hero.friction: No account · No download · A game in 10–15 minutes

showcase.caption: Real gameplay on the Modern Day globe — one of the maps below.

eras.heading: Choose Your Era
eras.globalDescription: Full-world maps spanning multiple continents and eras of history.
eras.regionalDescription: Theater-scale and alternate-history maps — from Civil War battlefields to flooded coastlines and indigenous polities — for faster, more intimate campaigns.

ancient.label: Ancient World
ancient.summary: The late classical world, when Rome, Parthia and Han China each ruled everything they could see. Fronts run from the Mediterranean through Persia to the Yellow River, with the open steppe behind all of them. Legion Tactics is the doctrine here: attack with three dice and you re-roll your lowest.

medieval.label: Medieval Era
medieval.summary: From the Crusades to the Mongol conquests, with kingdoms, caliphates and nomadic empires on one board. No era-wide doctrine applies, so the factions decide the shape of a game. The Mongol Khanate rolls an extra attack die, and Byzantine Greek Fire burns a unit off an attacker before the dice come out.

discovery.label: Age of Discovery
discovery.summary: The age of sail and gunpowder empires, fought over water as much as land. Sea Lanes caps an attack across water at two dice instead of three, so a crossing you would win on land is a gamble here. Portugal is the exception: its Naval Charts put the third die back.

ww2.label: World War II
ww2.summary: Industrial powers at war from the Atlantic to the Pacific, on a map drawn along the real front lines. Wartime Logistics lets you fortify twice in a turn, so your reserves can answer two theaters while other eras are still answering one.

coldwar.label: Cold War
coldwar.summary: NATO, the Warsaw Pact and the non-aligned world, contesting influence rather than ground. Influence Spread lets you spend three units from bordering territories to take a weak neighbour outright, no dice rolled, then waits three turns before you can do it again.

modern.label: The Modern Day
modern.summary: Contemporary superpowers and economic blocs on a board tuned for the 21st century. Precision Strike rewards mass over nibbling: commit four units or more and the attack rolls three dice.

acw.label: American Civil War
acw.summary: Union against Confederacy across the Eastern seaboard, the Mississippi and the western territories, on real state boundaries. Ties go to the defender everywhere else in the game. Rifle Doctrine re-rolls them, which makes attacking cost less here than anywhere.

risorgimento.label: Italian Unification
risorgimento.summary: Piedmont, the Two Sicilies and the papal middle, on real provincial outlines merged into regional theaters. The Carbonari Network reaches past your own border, so a province you do not touch can still change hands without a shot.

space_age.label: Space Age
space_age.summary: A projected world of 2100 with rising seas, coastal megacities, and a contested Moon. Research Lunar Expansion, build a Launch Pad, and launch a Space Station to project power into orbit. The Lunar Pioneers faction starts with Moon access; wonder builders may skip the station with a Space Elevator.

galaxy_age.label: Galactic Age — Coming Soon
galaxy_age.summary: Four worlds linked by hyperspace lanes: hold a gateway system and strike straight across its lane. Crossings roll fewer dice, so gateways defend like coasts — and each faction fights the lanes its own way.

getStarted.title: Jump In
getStarted.body: Jump straight in as a guest — no signup needed. A guest account stays in the browser you made it in; create a free account when you want your progress to follow you and to climb the leaderboards.

cta.heading: Ready to Command?
cta.noDownload: No download required. Play instantly in your browser.
